authority_citations.relevance: The current statute provides the off-site-delivery toll-free pharmacist-access pathway and separately requires the toll-free service number to be printed on a label affixed to each prescription-drug container dispensed to the patient.

Mass.gov identifies the current Board of Registration in Pharmacy professional-practice standards, dated December 6, 2024, as the operative regulation framework for pharmacy professional practice and patient counseling.

legal_reasoning: The frozen stem expressly states that the pharmacy is using the Massachusetts off-site-delivery pathway by providing access to a toll-free service connecting the patient with a pharmacist. Under the current text of M.G.L. c. 94C, § 21A, that pathway does not end with access to the service: the toll-free service number must also be printed on a label affixed to each prescription-drug container dispensed to the patient. Choice A states that additional step. Choices B and C place the number on different documents or packaging, choice D delays provision until after delivery, and choice E substitutes an ordinary local number; none satisfies the statutory container-label requirement. The existing answer A is therefore legally correct and the item is supportable as written.
